title.zh: 卷41 列傳第6 高熲 蘇威
title.en: Volume 41 Biographies 6: Gao Jiong, Su Wei

sentences.zh: 高熲高熲，字昭玄，一名敏，自雲渤海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong — Gao Jiong — styled Zhaoxuan, also called Min, claimed by his own account to be from the Bohai border district of Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong, whose courtesy name was Zhaoxuan and who was also known as Min, was a native of the Bohai frontier district, by his own account.

sentences.zh: 父賓，背齊歸周，大司馬獨孤信引為僚佐，賜姓獨孤氏。

translations.literal: His father Bin turned against Qi and submitted to Zhou; Grand Marshal Dugu Xin took him on as a staff officer and granted him the surname Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bin had abandoned Northern Qi for Northern Zhou, where Grand Marshal Dugu Xin recruited him to his staff and bestowed the surname Dugu upon him.

sentences.zh: 及信被誅，妻子徙蜀。

translations.literal: When Xin was executed, his wife and children were banished to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin was put to death, his family was sent into exile in Shu.

sentences.zh: 文獻皇后以賓父之故吏，每往來其家。

translations.literal: Empress Wenxian, because Bin had been a former subordinate of her father, often came and went at his household.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenxian — for Bin had once served under her father — was in the habit of visiting the Gao home.

sentences.zh: 賓後官至鄀州刺史，及熲貴，贈禮部尚書、渤海公。

translations.literal: Bin later reached the office of Governor of E Prefecture; when Jiong rose to eminence, Bin was posthumously made Minister of Rites and Duke of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Bin eventually rose to governor of Ezhou; once Jiong came to power, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites and Duke of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 熲少明敏，有器局，略涉書史，尤善詞令。

translations.literal: Jiong in youth was bright and keen, possessed breadth of vision, had some acquaintance with books and histories, and excelled especially at rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: From an early age Jiong was clever and quick-witted, with an expansive temperament; he dipped into the classics and histories and had a particular gift for eloquence.

sentences.zh: 初，孩孺時，家有柳樹，高百許尺，亭亭如蓋。

translations.literal: In his infancy the family had a willow tree, nearly a hundred feet tall, standing erect like a canopy.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still a child, the family had a willow tree nearly a hundred feet high, spreading like a great canopy.

sentences.zh: 裡中父老曰：「此家當出貴人。

translations.literal: The elders of the lane said: "This household will produce a man of rank."
translations.idiomatic: The elders of the neighborhood said, "This family is destined to produce a distinguished man."

sentences.zh: 」年十七，周齊王憲引為記室。

translations.literal: At seventeen, the Zhou Prince of Qi, Xian, took him on as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he was appointed recorder on the staff of Xian, Prince of Qi under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，襲爵武陽縣伯，除內史上士，尋遷下大夫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu he inherited the title Baron of Wuyang County, was appointed Inner Scribe Senior Clerk, and soon was promoted to Junior Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Zhou he succeeded to the barony of Wuyang and was named senior clerk in the Palace Secretariat, soon advancing to junior grand master.

sentences.zh: 以平齊功，拜開府。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Qi he was appointed General with an independent command.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in the conquest of Qi he was granted the privilege of an independent military establishment.

sentences.zh: 尋從越王盛擊隰州叛胡，平之。

translations.literal: Soon after he followed Prince Yue Sheng to attack the rebel Hu of Xi Prefecture and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Prince Yue Sheng on campaign against rebel Hu tribes in Xi Prefecture and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 高祖得政，素知熲強明，又習兵事，多計略，意欲引之入府，遣邗國公楊惠諭意。

translations.literal: When the Founder gained power, having long known Jiong's strength and clarity, and that he was versed in military affairs and rich in stratagems, he wished to draw him into the princely mansion and sent Duke of Han State Yang Hui to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wen seized control of the government, he already knew Jiong to be forceful and discerning, trained in warfare and full of stratagems, and wished to bring him into his staff; he sent Yang Hui, Duke of Han, to sound him out.

sentences.zh: 熲承旨欣然曰：「願受驅馳。

translations.literal: Jiong received the message and said gladly: "I am willing to be driven and spurred on."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong received the overture and replied with alacrity, "I am ready to serve at your command."

sentences.zh: 縱令公事不成，熲亦不辭滅族。

translations.literal: Even if the public affair should not succeed, Jiong would not decline extinction of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the enterprise should fail, I would not shrink from the destruction of my entire clan.

sentences.zh: 」於是為相府司錄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became Registrar of the princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon appointed registrar of the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 時長史鄭譯、司馬劉昉並以奢縱被疏，高祖彌屬意於熲，委以心膂。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Administrator Zheng Yi and Marshal Liu Fang were both estranged for extravagance and license; the Founder increasingly set his hopes on Jiong and entrusted him as heart and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chief administrator Zheng Yi and the marshal Liu Fang had both fallen from favor for their extravagance, and the prince relied on Jiong ever more closely as his trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 尉迥之起兵也，遣子惇率步騎八萬，進屯武陟。

translations.literal: When Yu Chi Jiong raised troops, he sent his son Dun leading eighty thousand foot and horse to advance and encamp at Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chi Jiong rebelled, he sent his son Dun at the head of eighty thousand infantry and cavalry to advance and encamp at Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 高祖令韋孝寬擊之，軍至河陽，莫敢先進。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered Wei Xiaokuan to attack him; the army reached Heyang, and none dared advance first.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ordered Wei Xiaokuan to attack him, but when the army reached Heyang no one dared to move forward.

sentences.zh: 高祖以諸將不一，令崔仲方監之，仲方辭父在山東。

translations.literal: The Founder, because the generals were not of one mind, ordered Cui Zhongfang to supervise them; Zhongfang declined on the ground that his father was in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Because the generals could not agree, the prince appointed Cui Zhongfang to supervise the campaign, but Zhongfang declined on the grounds that his father was still in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 時熲又見劉昉、鄭譯並無去意，遂自請行，深合上旨，遂遣熲。

translations.literal: At the time Jiong also saw that Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had no intention of going, and so volunteered to go himself; this deeply accorded with the Founder's intent, and he thereupon sent Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong saw that Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had no intention of taking the field, volunteered to go himself, and so won the prince's approval that he should be sent.

sentences.zh: 熲受命便發，遣人辭母，雲忠孝不可兩兼，歔欷就路。

translations.literal: Jiong received the order and set out at once, sent someone to take leave of his mother, saying loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled, and went on his way with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong accepted the commission and set out at once, sending word to his mother that loyalty and filial duty could not both be satisfied, and departed with tears.

sentences.zh: 至軍，為橋于沁水，賊於上流縱大栰，熲預為土狗以禦之。

translations.literal: On reaching the army he built a bridge on the Qin River; the rebels upstream released great rafts, and Jiong had prepared earthen dikes to ward them off.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the army he built a bridge across the Qin River; when the rebels upstream sent great rafts downstream, Jiong had already prepared earthen barriers to block them.

sentences.zh: 既渡，焚橋而戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Having crossed, he burned the bridge and fought, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Once across, he burned the bridge and gave battle, winning a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 遂至鄴下，與迥交戰，仍共宇文忻、李詢等設策，因平尉迥。

translations.literal: He then reached below Ye, fought with Jiong, and together with Yuwen Xin, Li Xun, and others devised stratagems, thereby pacifying Yu Chi Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Ye, fought Yu Chi Jiong there, and together with Yuwen Xin, Li Xun, and others laid plans that brought about the suppression of the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 軍還，侍宴於臥內，上撤禦帷以賜之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he attended a feast in the sleeping quarters; the sovereign removed the imperial curtain and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was entertained at a feast in the prince's private quarters, and the prince removed the imperial curtain and gave it to him as a gift.

sentences.zh: 進位柱國，改封義寧縣公，遷相府司馬，任寄益隆。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Pillar of State, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yining County, he was transferred to Marshal of the princely mansion, and his commission grew ever more weighty.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to pillar of state, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yining County, made marshal of the prince's household, and entrusted with ever greater authority.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜尚書左僕射，兼納言，進封渤海郡公，朝臣莫與為比，上每呼為獨孤而不名也。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Jiong was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, advanced to Duke of Bohai Commandery; no courtier could be compared with him, and the sovereign always called him Dugu and never by name.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Jiong was appointed left vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent censor-in-chief, and advanced to Duke of Bohai; no minister could rival him, and the emperor always addressed him as "Dugu" rather than by his personal name.

sentences.zh: 熲深避權勢，上表遜位，讓于蘇威。

translations.literal: Jiong deeply shunned power and position, submitted a memorial yielding his post, and yielded to Su Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong deliberately kept his distance from overt power, memorialized to resign his office, and recommended Su Wei in his place.

sentences.zh: 上欲成其美，聽解僕射。

translations.literal: The sovereign wished to complete his excellence and permitted him to relinquish the vice directorship.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to honor his magnanimity and allowed him to step down as vice director.

sentences.zh: 數日，上曰：「蘇威高蹈前朝，熲能推舉。

translations.literal: After several days the sovereign said: "Su Wei walked loftily in the previous dynasty, and Jiong was able to recommend him."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor said, "Su Wei was a man of lofty principle under the previous dynasty, and Jiong had the discernment to recommend him."

sentences.zh: 吾聞進賢受上賞，寧可令去官！

translations.literal: I have heard that recommending the worthy receives the highest reward — how could I let him leave office!"
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that he who advances the worthy earns the highest reward — how could I allow him to leave his post!"

sentences.zh: 」於是命熲復位。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Jiong to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered Jiong to resume his office.

sentences.zh: 俄拜左衛大將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, his original offices remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named general-in-chief of the Left Guard while retaining his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為寇患，詔熲鎮遏緣邊。

translations.literal: At the time the Turks repeatedly caused border raids; an edict ordered Jiong to garrison and restrain the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: As the Turks were raiding the borders repeatedly, the emperor ordered Jiong to take command of frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 及還，賜馬百余匹，牛羊千計。

translations.literal: On his return he was given more than a hundred horses and cattle and sheep by the thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was rewarded with more than a hundred horses and thousands of head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 領新都大監，制度多出於熲。

translations.literal: He headed the Grand Supervisor of the New Capital; regulations and systems mostly came from Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: As superintendent of the new capital, he oversaw institutions and regulations that owed much to his own design.

sentences.zh: 熲每坐朝堂北槐樹下以聽事，其樹不依行列，有司將伐之。

translations.literal: Jiong each day sat under the northern locust tree of the audience hall to hear business; the tree did not follow the rows, and the relevant offices were about to cut it down.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong habitually conducted business seated beneath the locust tree north of the audience hall; because the tree did not align with the planted rows, the authorities were about to have it felled.

sentences.zh: 上特命勿去，以示後人。

translations.literal: The sovereign specially ordered that it not be removed, to show posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor expressly forbade its removal, as a mark for future generations.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree to which he was esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 又拜左領軍大將軍，余官如故。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Army, his other offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed general-in-chief of the Left Army while his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，二旬起令視事。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office; after twenty days he was recalled to attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother, but after only twenty days was ordered back to duty.

sentences.zh: 熲流涕辭讓，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Jiong with flowing tears declined and yielded; an excellent edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong tearfully protested, but a gracious edict would not allow him to refuse.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，長孫覽、元景山等伐陳，令熲節度諸軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, Changsun Lan, Yuan Jingshan, and others attacked Chen; Jiong was ordered to command all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang, when Changsun Lan, Yuan Jingshan, and others campaigned against Chen, Jiong was placed in overall command of the forces.

sentences.zh: 會陳宣帝薨，熲以禮不伐喪，奏請班師。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Xuan of Chen died; Jiong, on the ground that by ritual one does not attack during mourning, memorialized requesting withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Chen died, Jiong argued that propriety forbade campaigning during a period of mourning and memorialized for the army to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 蕭岩之叛也，詔熲綏集江漢，甚得人和。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan rebelled, an edict ordered Jiong to pacify and gather the Jiang and Han regions; he greatly won the harmony of the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan rebelled, the emperor ordered Jiong to restore order along the Yangtze and Han, and he won the people's loyalty with notable success.

sentences.zh: 上嘗問熲取陳之策，熲曰：「江北地寒，田收差晚，江南土熱，水田早熟。

translations.literal: The sovereign once asked Jiong for a strategy to take Chen; Jiong said: "North of the river the land is cold and the harvest is rather late; south of the river the soil is warm and the paddy fields ripen early."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Jiong for a plan to conquer Chen. Jiong replied, "The north is cold and the harvest comes late; the south is warm and the rice ripens early."

sentences.zh: 量彼收積之際，微征士馬，聲言掩襲。

translations.literal: Gauge the time of their harvest and collection, lightly levy troops and horses, and proclaim a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of their harvest season, send a small force and announce a surprise raid."

sentences.zh: 彼必屯兵禦守，足得廢其農時。

translations.literal: They will surely mass troops to defend, which will suffice to waste their agricultural season.
translations.idiomatic: They will mass troops to defend, and that alone will ruin their farming season."

sentences.zh: 彼既聚兵，我便解甲，再三若此，賊以為常。

translations.literal: Once they have gathered troops, we then dismiss our armor; if this is done again and again, the enemy will take it as routine.
translations.idiomatic: Once they have mobilized, we stand down; repeat this several times until the enemy treats it as routine."

sentences.zh: 後更集兵，彼必不信，猶豫之頃，我乃濟師，登陸而戰，兵氣益倍。

translations.literal: Later when we again gather troops, they will surely not believe it; in the moment of their hesitation we then cross the army over, land and fight, and the army's spirit will be doubled.
translations.idiomatic: When we mobilize again they will not believe us; in their hesitation we cross in earnest, land, and fight — and our troops' morale will be doubled."

sentences.zh: 又江南土薄，舍多竹茅，所有儲積，皆非地窖。

translations.literal: Moreover south of the river the soil is thin, dwellings are mostly bamboo and thatch, and all stored goods are not in underground cellars.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the south has thin soil and houses mostly of bamboo and thatch; grain stores are not kept in underground cellars."

sentences.zh: 密遣行人，因風縱火，待彼修立，複更燒之。

translations.literal: Secretly send agents, and when the wind serves set fires; wait until they have rebuilt, then burn again.
translations.idiomatic: Send agents secretly to set fires when the wind is right; when they rebuild, burn them again."

sentences.zh: 不出數年，自可財力俱盡。

translations.literal: Within a few years, of themselves wealth and strength will both be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years their wealth and strength will be exhausted of themselves."

sentences.zh: 」上行其策，由是陳人益敝。

translations.literal: The sovereign carried out his strategy, and thereby the people of Chen grew ever more depleted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted his plan, and the people of Chen grew steadily weaker.

sentences.zh: 九年，晉王廣大舉伐陳，以熲為元帥長史，三軍諮稟，皆取斷於熲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Prince Jin Guang mounted a great campaign against Chen; Jiong was made chief clerk to the commander-in-chief, and all three armies' consultations and reports were decided by Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Prince Jin launched a major campaign against Chen, Jiong served as chief of staff to the commander; every military decision passed through him.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，晉王欲納陳主寵姬張麗華。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, Prince Jin wished to take Zhang Lihua, the Chen ruler's favored consort.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell, Prince Jin wished to take Zhang Lihua, the late ruler's favorite consort, for himself.

sentences.zh: 熲曰：「武王滅殷，戮妲己。

translations.literal: Jiong said: "When King Wu destroyed Yin, he executed Daji."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said, "When King Wu overthrew the Shang, he executed Daji."

sentences.zh: 今平陳國，不宜取麗華。

translations.literal: Now that Chen has been pacified, it is not fitting to take Lihua.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have conquered Chen, Lihua must not be taken."

sentences.zh: 」乃命斬之，王甚不悅。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered her beheaded; the prince was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered her executed, to the prince's deep displeasure.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，以功加授上柱國，進爵齊國公，賜物九千段，定食千乘縣千五百戶。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for merit he was further appointed Supreme Pillar of State, advanced to Duke of Qi State, given nine thousand bolts of goods, and granted a fief of one thousand five hundred households in Qiansheng County.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was further promoted to supreme pillar of state and advanced to Duke of Qi, with nine thousand rolls of silk and a fief of fifteen hundred households in Qiansheng County.

sentences.zh: 上因勞之曰：「公伐陳後，人言公反，朕已斬之。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereupon comforted him, saying: "After you attacked Chen, men said you would rebel; I have already beheaded them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consoled him, saying, "After your campaign against Chen, some said you would rebel — I have already had them executed."

sentences.zh: 君臣道合，非青蠅所間也。

translations.literal: Sovereign and minister are united in the Way — it is not for bluebottle flies to come between.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between sovereign and minister is sound; no whispering slanderer can come between us."

sentences.zh: 」熲又遜位，詔曰：「公識鑒通遠，器略優深，出參戎律，廓清淮海，入司禁旅，實委心腹。

translations.literal: Jiong again yielded his post; an edict said: "Your discernment reaches far, your capacity and strategy are superior and deep; going out you joined in military regulations and cleared the Huai and sea regions; entering you managed the forbidden guard — truly you were entrusted as heart and belly."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong again offered to resign. The edict read, "Your judgment is far-reaching and your talent profound; abroad you directed the armies and cleared the Huai region, at court you commanded the palace guard — you have been my true right hand."

sentences.zh: 自朕受命，常典機衡，竭誠陳力，心跡俱盡。

translations.literal: Since I received the Mandate you have constantly held the keys of state, exhausted sincerity and displayed strength, heart and tracks both fully spent.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne you have held the reins of government, serving with complete loyalty — in intent and in deed alike."

sentences.zh: 此則天降良輔，翊贊朕躬，幸無詞費也。

translations.literal: This is Heaven sending a fine assistant to aid and support my person — I hope you will not waste words."
translations.idiomatic: You are a minister sent by Heaven to support my rule — spare me further protestations."

sentences.zh: 」其優獎如此。

translations.literal: Such was the excellence of his rewards and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the honors he received.

sentences.zh: 是後右衛將軍龐晃及將軍盧賁等，前後短熲於上。

translations.literal: After this Right Guard General Pang Huang and General Lu Ben and others, one after another, spoke ill of Jiong to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Pang Huang, general of the Right Guard, and the general Lu Ben, among others, repeatedly slandered Jiong to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上怒之，皆被疏黜。

translations.literal: The sovereign was angry with them; all were estranged and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and had them all dismissed from favor.

sentences.zh: 因謂熲曰：「獨孤公猶鏡也，每被磨瑩，皎然益明。

translations.literal: He thereupon said to Jiong: "Duke Dugu is like a mirror — each time it is ground and polished, it grows brighter and clearer."
translations.idiomatic: He then told Jiong, "Duke Dugu, you are like a mirror: every time it is polished, it shines the brighter."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，尚書都事姜曄、楚州行參軍李君才並奏稱水旱不調，罪由高熲，請廢黜之。

translations.literal: Before long, Department of State Affairs Chief Clerk Jiang Ye and Chuzhou Acting Staff Officer Li Juncai both memorialized saying flood and drought were not in harmony, the fault lay with Gao Jiong, and requested his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Jiang Ye of the Secretariat and Li Juncai, acting staff officer of Chuzhou, both memorialized that floods and droughts were out of balance and blamed Gao Jiong, asking that he be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 二人俱得罪而去，親禮逾密。

translations.literal: Both men were punished and left; intimate courtesy grew ever closer.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were punished and dismissed, while the emperor's intimacy with Jiong grew ever closer.

sentences.zh: 上幸并州，留熲居守。

translations.literal: The sovereign visited Bingzhou and left Jiong to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Bingzhou, he left Jiong in charge of the capital.

sentences.zh: 及上還京，賜縑五千匹，複賜行宮一所，以為莊舍。

translations.literal: When the sovereign returned to the capital, he gave five thousand bolts of silk and again bestowed one traveling palace as a manor estate.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital the emperor gave him five thousand bolts of silk and a traveling palace to serve as a country estate.

sentences.zh: 其夫人賀拔氏寢疾，中使顧問，絡繹不絕。

translations.literal: His wife the Lady Heluo was ill in bed; palace envoys inquired after her in an unbroken stream.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife Lady Heluo fell ill, palace envoys inquired after her without cease.

sentences.zh: 上親幸其第，賜錢百萬，絹萬匹，複賜以千里馬。

translations.literal: The sovereign personally visited his residence, gave a million in cash, ten thousand bolts of silk, and again bestowed a thousand-li horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited his home in person, gave him a million in cash and ten thousand bolts of silk, and presented him with a horse of legendary stamina.

sentences.zh: 上嘗從容命熲與賀若弼言及平陳事，熲曰：「賀若弼先獻十策，後於蔣山苦戰破賊。

translations.literal: The sovereign once at leisure ordered Jiong and He Ruo Bi to speak of the pacification of Chen; Jiong said: "He Ruo Bi first offered ten stratagems, then at Mount Jiang fought bitterly and broke the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Jiong and He Ruo Bi to discuss the conquest of Chen. Jiong said, "He Ruo Bi first offered ten stratagems, then fought a hard battle at Mount Jiang and broke the enemy."

sentences.zh: 臣文吏耳，焉敢與大將軍論功！

translations.literal: Your servant is a civil clerk — how dare he discuss merit with a great general!"
translations.idiomatic: I am only a civil official — how dare I dispute merit with a great general!"

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑，時論嘉其有讓。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly; opinion of the time praised his modesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily, and contemporaries praised his humility.

sentences.zh: 尋以其子表仁取太子勇女，前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Soon his son Biaoren took the daughter of Crown Prince Yong; rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his son Biaoren married the daughter of Crown Prince Yong, and the rewards that followed were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 時熒惑入太微，犯左執法。

translations.literal: At the time Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure and encroached on the Left Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure and trespassed upon the asterism of the Left Enforcer.

sentences.zh: 術者劉暉私言於熲曰：「天文不利宰相，可修德以禳之。

translations.literal: The diviner Liu Hui privately spoke to Jiong, saying: "The heavens are unfavorable to the chief minister — you may cultivate virtue to avert it."
translations.idiomatic: The astrologer Liu Hui told Jiong privately, "The stars are unfavorable to the chief minister; cultivate virtue to avert calamity."

sentences.zh: 」熲不自安，以暉言奏之。

translations.literal: Jiong was not at ease in himself and reported Hui's words to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Jiong reported Liu Hui's words to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上厚加賞慰。

translations.literal: The sovereign richly added rewards and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded and reassured him generously.

sentences.zh: 突厥犯塞，以熲為元帥，擊賊破之。

translations.literal: The Turks raided the border; Jiong was made commander-in-chief, attacked the bandits and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier, Jiong was made commander-in-chief, attacked them, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又出白道，進圖入磧，遣使請兵。

translations.literal: He again went out by the White Road, advanced planning to enter the desert, and sent envoys requesting troops.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced by the White Road with plans to penetrate the desert and sent envoys requesting reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 近臣緣此言熲欲反，上未有所答，熲亦破賊而還。

translations.literal: Close ministers on this basis said Jiong wished to rebel; the sovereign had not yet replied when Jiong also defeated the bandits and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Court intimates seized on this to accuse Jiong of plotting rebellion; before the emperor could respond, Jiong had already defeated the enemy and returned.

sentences.zh: 時太子勇失愛於上，潛有廢立之意。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Yong had lost the sovereign's favor; secretly there was intent to depose and establish.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong had by then fallen from the emperor's favor, and the emperor was quietly considering replacing him.

sentences.zh: 謂熲曰：「晉王妃有神憑之，言王必有天下，若之何？

translations.literal: He said to Jiong: "The Jin prince's consort has a spirit possessing her, saying the prince must have all under Heaven — what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: He said to Jiong, "Prince Jin's consort is possessed by a spirit that says the prince is destined to rule the realm — what should be done?"

sentences.zh: 」熲長跪曰：「長幼有序，其可廢乎！

translations.literal: Jiong knelt long and said: "Elder and younger have an order — how can he be deposed!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong knelt and said, "Elder and younger have their proper order — how can the heir be set aside!"

sentences.zh: 」上默然而止，獨孤皇后知熲不可奪，陰欲去之，夫人卒，後言於上曰：「高僕射老矣，而喪夫人，陛下何能不為之娶！

translations.literal: The sovereign silently stopped; Empress Dugu knew Jiong could not be swayed and secretly wished to remove him. When the lady died, the empress spoke to the sovereign, saying: "Vice Director Gao is old, and has lost his wife — how can Your Majesty not find him a wife!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent and dropped the matter. Empress Dugu, knowing Jiong could not be won over, secretly wished to remove him. When his wife died, she said to the emperor, "Vice Director Gao is growing old and has lost his wife — surely Your Majesty should find him a new one!"

sentences.zh: 」上以後言謂熲，熲流涕謝曰：「臣今已老，退朝之後，唯齋居讀佛經而已。

translations.literal: The sovereign spoke to Jiong with the empress's words; Jiong with flowing tears declined, saying: "Your servant is now old; after leaving court, he only fasts in seclusion and reads Buddhist sutras."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeated the empress's suggestion to Jiong, who tearfully replied, "I am old now; after court I devote myself only to fasting and reading the Buddhist sutras."

sentences.zh: 雖陛下垂哀之深，至於納室，非臣所願。

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty's compassion runs deep, as for taking a new chamber, it is not your servant's wish.
translations.idiomatic: However deep Your Majesty's kindness, taking a new wife is not what I wish."

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 至是，熲愛妾產男，上聞之極歡，後甚不悅。

translations.literal: At this time Jiong's beloved concubine bore a son; the sovereign heard and was extremely pleased; the empress was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jiong's favorite concubine had borne a son; the emperor was delighted to hear it, but the empress was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 上問其故，後曰：「陛下當覆信高熲邪？

translations.literal: The sovereign asked the reason; the empress said: "Does Your Majesty still trust Gao Jiong again?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, the empress said, "Can Your Majesty still trust Gao Jiong?"

sentences.zh: 始陛下欲為熲娶，熲心存愛妾，面欺陛下。

translations.literal: At first when Your Majesty wished to find Jiong a wife, Jiong harbored his beloved concubine in his heart and deceived Your Majesty to his face.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty offered to find him a wife, he already kept a favorite concubine and lied to your face."

sentences.zh: 今其詐已見，陛下安得信之！

translations.literal: Now his deceit has appeared — how can Your Majesty trust him!"
translations.idiomatic: Now his deception is plain — how can Your Majesty trust him!"

sentences.zh: 」上由是疏熲。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereby grew estranged from Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the emperor grew distant from Jiong.

sentences.zh: 會議伐遼東，熲固諫不可。

translations.literal: When there was discussion of campaigning against Liaodong, Jiong firmly remonstrated that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated a campaign against Liaodong, Jiong strongly advised against it.

sentences.zh: 上不從，以熲為元帥長史，從漢王征遼東，遇霖潦疾疫，不利而還。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not follow his advice; Jiong was made chief clerk to the commander-in-chief and followed Prince Han on the Liaodong campaign; they met heavy rains, floods, and epidemic, and returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor overruled him, made Jiong chief of staff on the Liaodong campaign under Prince Han, and the army turned back defeated by floods, rains, and plague.

sentences.zh: 後言於上曰：「熲初不欲行，陛下強遣之，妾固知其無功矣。

translations.literal: Later she spoke to the sovereign, saying: "Jiong at first did not wish to go; Your Majesty forced him to go — your servant knew all along he would have no success."
translations.idiomatic: The empress later told the emperor, "Jiong never wanted to go — you sent him against his will, and I knew from the start the campaign would fail."

sentences.zh: 」又上以漢王年少，專委軍於熲。

translations.literal: Moreover the sovereign, because Prince Han was young, specially entrusted the army to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor moreover, considering Prince Han young, placed the entire army under Jiong's command.

sentences.zh: 熲以任寄隆重，每懷至公，無自疑之意。

translations.literal: Jiong, because his commission was weighty and solemn, always harbored utmost impartiality and had no thought of self-doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong bore his heavy responsibility with scrupulous impartiality and never wavered in his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 諒所言多不用，甚銜之。

translations.literal: Liang's words were mostly not adopted, and he deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Han found his counsel largely ignored and grew deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 及還，諒泣言於後曰：「兒倖免高熲所殺。

translations.literal: On returning, Liang wept and spoke to the empress, saying: "Your son narrowly escaped being killed by Gao Jiong."
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, the prince tearfully told the empress, "Your son was nearly killed by Gao Jiong."

sentences.zh: 」上聞之，彌不平。

translations.literal: The sovereign heard this and grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, his displeasure deepened.

sentences.zh: 俄而上柱國王世積以罪誅，當推核之際，乃有宮禁中事，雲於熲處得之。

translations.literal: Before long Supreme Pillar of State Wang Shiji was executed for a crime; at the time of investigation there were matters from within the palace forbidden precinct, said to have been obtained from Jiong's place.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Shiji, supreme pillar of state, was executed; during the investigation palace secrets were traced to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 上欲成熲之罪，聞此大驚。

translations.literal: The sovereign wished to complete Jiong's guilt; on hearing this he was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, intent on convicting Jiong, was shocked by this discovery.

sentences.zh: 時上柱國賀若弼、吳州總管宇文彌、刑部尚書薛胄、民部尚書斛律孝卿、兵部尚書柳述等明熲無罪，上逾怒，皆以之屬吏。

translations.literal: At the time Supreme Pillar of State He Ruo Bi, Wuzhou Regional Inspector Yuwen Mi, Minister of Justice Xue Zhou, Minister of Revenue Hulu Xiaqing, Minister of War Liu Shu, and others made clear Jiong was guiltless; the sovereign grew ever angrier and all were handed over to the law officers.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi, Yuwen Mi, Xue Zhou, Hulu Xiaqing, Liu Shu, and others spoke up for Jiong's innocence; the emperor flew into a rage and had them all arrested.

sentences.zh: 自是朝臣莫敢言者。

translations.literal: From this time no courtier dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one at court dared speak on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 熲竟坐免，以公就第。

translations.literal: Jiong in the end was convicted and dismissed, and as duke returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was at last removed from office and sent home, retaining only his ducal title.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上幸秦王俊第，召熲侍宴。

translations.literal: Before long the sovereign visited the residence of Prince Qin Jun and summoned Jiong to attend the feast.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, during a visit to Prince Qin Jun's mansion, the emperor summoned Jiong to join the banquet.

sentences.zh: 熲歔欷悲不自勝，獨狐皇后亦對之泣，左右皆流涕。

translations.literal: Jiong sobbed and could not master his grief; Empress Dugu also wept facing him; those at left and right all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong wept uncontrollably; Empress Dugu wept as she faced him, and everyone present was in tears.

sentences.zh: 上謂熲曰：「朕不負公，公自負也。

translations.literal: The sovereign said to Jiong: "I have not failed you — you have failed yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "I have not failed you — you have failed yourself."

sentences.zh: 」因謂侍臣曰：「我于高熲勝兒子，雖或不見，常似目前。

translations.literal: He thereupon said to the attending ministers: "I surpass a son in my regard for Gao Jiong; though I may not see him, he is always as before my eyes."
translations.idiomatic: He told the ministers, "I cherished Gao Jiong more than a son; though I might not see him, he was always before my eyes."

sentences.zh: 自其解落，瞑然忘之，如本無高熲。

translations.literal: "Since he was dismissed, I have forgotten him in darkness, as though there had never been a Gao Jiong."
translations.idiomatic: "Since his dismissal I have put him out of mind, as if he had never existed."

sentences.zh: 不可以身要君，自雲第一也。

translations.literal: "One must not use one's person to demand things of the sovereign, or claim for oneself that one is first."
translations.idiomatic: "A minister must not hold the sovereign hostage to his own importance or boast that he is indispensable."
(Close of quotation.)

sentences.zh: 頃之，熲國令上熲陰事，稱：「其子表仁謂熲曰：'司馬仲達初托疾不朝，遂有天下。

translations.literal: Before long Jiong's estate steward reported Jiong's secret affairs, saying: "His son Biaoren said to Jiong: 'Sima Yi at first feigned illness and did not attend court, and in the end possessed all under Heaven.'"
translations.idiomatic: Soon his estate steward denounced him, reporting that his son Biaoren had said to him, "Sima Yi feigned illness and stayed away from court — and in the end seized the realm."

sentences.zh: 公今遇此，焉知非福！

translations.literal: "You now meet this — how do you know it is not fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: "You are in the same position now — who is to say this is not a blessing in disguise?"

sentences.zh: '」於是上大怒，囚熲于內史省而鞫之。

translations.literal: "Thereupon the sovereign was greatly enraged, imprisoned Jiong in the Ministry of the Interior, and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, imprisoned Jiong in the Ministry of the Interior, and put him on trial.

sentences.zh: 憲司複奏熲他事，雲：「沙門真覺嘗謂熲雲：'明年國有大喪。

translations.literal: The law officers again memorialized other matters concerning Jiong, saying: "The monk Zhenjue once told Jiong: 'Next year the state will have a great mourning.'"
translations.idiomatic: The prosecutors added further charges: the monk Zhenjue had told Jiong, "Next year the state will mourn a great death."

sentences.zh: '尼令暉複雲：'十七、十八年，皇帝有大厄。

translations.literal: "The nun Linghui again said: 'In the seventeenth and eighteenth years the emperor will suffer a great calamity."
translations.idiomatic: "The nun Linghui had also said, "In the seventeenth and eighteenth years the emperor will face grave peril."

sentences.zh: 十九年不可過。

translations.literal: "The nineteenth year cannot be passed."
translations.idiomatic: "He will not survive the nineteenth year."

sentences.zh: '上聞而益怒，顧謂群臣曰：「帝王豈可力求！

translations.literal: "The sovereign heard and grew ever angrier, turned to the assembled ministers and said: "Can an emperor's throne be striven for by force!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, hearing this, turned to the court and exclaimed, "Does anyone think the throne can be seized by scheming!"

sentences.zh: 孔子以大聖之才，作法垂世，寧不欲大位邪？

translations.literal: "Confucius, with the talent of the greatest sage, established law to last through the ages — would he not have desired the supreme position?"
translations.idiomatic: "Confucius, for all his sagehood, laid down laws for the ages — would he not have wanted the throne?"

sentences.zh: 天命不可耳。

translations.literal: "It was only that the Mandate of Heaven did not allow it."
translations.idiomatic: "Only the Mandate of Heaven denied it to him."

sentences.zh: 熲與子言，自比晉帝，此何心乎？

translations.literal: "Jiong spoke with his son and compared himself to the Jin emperor — what sort of heart is this?"
translations.idiomatic: "Jiong spoke to his son and likened himself to an emperor of Jin — what treason is this?"

sentences.zh: 」有司請斬熲。

translations.literal: "The relevant offices requested Jiong be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The judges asked that Jiong be executed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「去年殺虞慶則，今茲斬王世積，如更誅熲，天下其謂我何？

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Last year I killed Yu Qingze; this year I beheaded Wang Shiji — if I also execute Jiong, what will all under Heaven say of me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Last year I killed Yu Qingze, this year Wang Shiji — if I kill Jiong as well, what will the world say of me?"

sentences.zh: 」於是除名為民。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he was stripped of name and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore stripped of rank and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 熲初為僕射，其母誡之曰：「汝富貴已極，但有一斫頭耳，爾宜慎之！

translations.literal: When Jiong first became Vice Director, his mother admonished him, saying: "Your wealth and honor have already reached the limit — there is only one thing left, a beheading — you should be careful!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong first became vice director, his mother warned him, "You have risen as high as a man can — only the executioner's blade remains; take care!"

sentences.zh: 」熲由是常恐禍變。

translations.literal: Jiong thereby constantly feared calamity and change.
translations.idiomatic: From that time he lived in constant fear of disaster.

sentences.zh: 及此，熲歡然無恨色，以為得免於禍。

translations.literal: At this, Jiong was pleased and had no look of resentment, thinking he had escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Now he accepted his punishment without bitterness, believing he had escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，拜為太常。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Jiong was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Jiong was appointed minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時詔收周、齊故樂人及天下散樂。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered the collection of former Zhou and Qi musicians and scattered performers throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out to gather musicians of the former Zhou and Qi dynasties and performers scattered across the empire.

sentences.zh: 熲奏曰：「此樂久廢。

translations.literal: Jiong memorialized, saying: "This music has long been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong memorialized, "This music has long fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 今或征之，恐無識之徒棄本逐末，遞相教習。

translations.literal: "If it is now summoned, I fear men without understanding will abandon their proper work and pursue the secondary, teaching one another in turn."
translations.idiomatic: "To revive it now may lead the ignorant to abandon their proper occupations and teach one another frivolous arts instead."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: The sovereign was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 帝時侈靡，聲色滋甚，又起長城之役。

translations.literal: The sovereign at the time was extravagant and dissolute, sounds and colors daily increased, and he again launched the Great Wall labor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was growing ever more extravagant, indulging in music and spectacle, and launched the Great Wall project.

sentences.zh: 熲甚病之，謂太常丞李懿曰：「周天元以好樂而亡，殷鑒不遙，安可複爾！

translations.literal: Jiong was greatly grieved by this and said to Vice Director of Ceremonies Li Yi: "The Zhou Emperor Yuan perished through love of music; the Yin mirror is not far — how can we repeat this!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was deeply troubled and told Vice Director Li Yi, "Emperor Yuan of Northern Zhou ruined his state through music — that lesson is recent; how can we repeat it!"

sentences.zh: 」時帝遇啟民可汗恩禮過厚，熲謂太府卿何稠曰：「此虜頗知中國虛實、山川險易，恐為後患。

translations.literal: "At the time the sovereign treated Qimin Khan with excessive favor; Jiong said to Minister of the Palace Treasury He Chou: "This barbarian knows well the emptiness and fullness of China, the mountains and rivers and their passes — I fear he will be a later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was lavishing honors on Qimin Khan; Jiong told Minister He Chou, "This barbarian knows our strengths and weaknesses, our terrain and defenses — he may become a future threat."

sentences.zh: 」複謂觀王雄曰：「近來朝廷殊無綱紀。

translations.literal: He again said to Prince Guan Xiong: "Recently the court has had no discipline at all."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Prince Guan Xiong, "The court lately has no discipline whatsoever."

sentences.zh: 」有人奏之，帝以為謗訕朝政，於是下詔誅之，諸子徙邊。

translations.literal: Someone reported this; the sovereign thought it slandered and mocked court administration, and thereupon issued an edict executing him; his sons were banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported, the emperor treated it as slander of the government, issued an edict for his execution, and banished his sons to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 熲有文武大略，明達世務。

translations.literal: Jiong had civil and military great strategy, clear penetration of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong possessed great talent in civil and military affairs and a clear grasp of public business.

sentences.zh: 及蒙任寄之後，竭誠盡節，進引貞良，以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Once he received weighty commission, he exhausted loyalty and fulfilled duty, advanced and introduced the upright and good, and took all under Heaven as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Once entrusted with power, he served with complete loyalty, promoted worthy men, and treated the welfare of the realm as his personal responsibility.

sentences.zh: 蘇威、楊素、賀若弼、韓擒等，皆熲所推薦，各盡其用，為一代名臣。

translations.literal: Su Wei, Yang Su, He Ruo Bi, Han Qin, and others were all recommended by Jiong; each fulfilled his use and became famous ministers of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Yang Su, He Ruo Bi, Han Qin, and others were all men he had advanced; each rose to eminence as a statesman of the age.

sentences.zh: 自余立功立事者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Besides these, those who established merit and affairs cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them, the men who won distinction under his patronage are beyond number.

sentences.zh: 當朝執政將二十年，朝野推服，物無異議。

translations.literal: He held court power for nearly twenty years; court and countryside submitted to him, and on material things there was no dissenting voice.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he dominated the government; court and country deferred to him without dispute.

sentences.zh: 治致升平，熲之力也，論者以為真宰相。

translations.literal: He governed to the point of ascending peace — this was Jiong's strength; opinion holders considered him a true chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The era of peace and order was largely his achievement, and contemporaries regarded him as a true prime minister.

sentences.zh: 及其被誅，天下莫不傷惜，至今稱冤不已。

translations.literal: When he was executed, all under Heaven none did not grieve and pity him; to this day they call his case unjust without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: At his execution the empire mourned him; to this day his name is invoked as a wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 所有奇策密謀及損益時政，熲皆削稿，世無知者。

translations.literal: All ingenious stratagems and secret plans and matters of benefit and harm to government of the time — Jiong all cut the drafts, and the age has no knowledge of them.
translations.idiomatic: The clever stratagems and secret policy papers he drafted were all destroyed by his own hand, and the world never knew them.

sentences.zh: 其子盛道，官至莒州刺史，徙柳城而卒。

translations.literal: His son Shengdong reached the office of Governor of Ju Prefecture, was banished to Liucheng and died there.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shengdong rose to governor of Ju Prefecture, was exiled to Liucheng, and died there.

sentences.zh: 次弘德，封應國公，晉王府記室。

translations.literal: The second, Hongde, was enfeoffed Duke of Ying State and served as recorder to the Prince of Jin's household.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Hongde was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying and served as recorder to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 次表仁，封渤海郡公，徙蜀郡。

translations.literal: The third, Biaoren, was enfeoffed Duke of Bohai Commandery and was banished to Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Biaoren was enfeoffed Duke of Bohai and exiled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 蘇威蘇威，字無畏，京兆武功人也。

translations.literal: Su Wei — Su Wei — styled Wuwai, was a man of Wugong in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, whose courtesy name was Wuwai, was a native of Wugong in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 父綽，魏度支尚書。

translations.literal: His father Chuo was Wei Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuo had been director of revenue under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 威少有至性，五歲喪父，哀毀有若成人。

translations.literal: Wei from youth had utmost nature; at five he lost his father, and his mourning destruction was as if he were an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Wei from childhood showed exceptional filial devotion; when he lost his father at five, he mourned with the gravity of an adult.

sentences.zh: 周太祖時，襲爵美陽縣公，仕郡功曹。

translations.literal: Under Zhou Emperor Taizu he inherited the title Duke of Meiyang County and served as Merit Officer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizu of Zhou he inherited the dukedom of Meiyang and served as merit officer in his commandery.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護見而禮之，以其女新興主妻焉。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of War Yuwen Hu saw him and treated him with ceremony, marrying him to his daughter the Princess Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Yuwen Hu received him with honor and gave him his daughter, Princess Xinxing, in marriage.

sentences.zh: 見護專權，恐禍及己，逃入山中，為叔父所逼，卒不獲免。

translations.literal: Seeing Hu's monopoly of power, he feared calamity would reach himself, fled into the mountains, was compelled by his uncle, and in the end could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Hu's monopoly of power, he fled into the mountains to escape the coming disaster, but was forced back by his uncle and could not get free.

sentences.zh: 然威每屏居山寺，以諷讀為娛。

translations.literal: Yet Wei often secluded himself in mountain temples, taking sutra recitation as his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless he often withdrew to mountain monasteries and amused himself by chanting sutras.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，改封懷道縣公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Three Ranks, his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Huaidao County.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed bearer of the staff of authority, general of chariots and cavalry, equal in three ranks, and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Huaidao.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，拜稍伯下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, he was appointed Junior Grand Master of Shaobo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took personal control of government, he was named junior grand master of Shaobo.

sentences.zh: 前後所授，並辭疾不拜。

translations.literal: The offices conferred before and after, he all declined on grounds of illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined every appointment on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 有從父妹者，適河南元雄。

translations.literal: He had a cousin sister who was married to Yuan Xiong of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a cousin who had married Yuan Xiong of Henan.

sentences.zh: 雄先與突厥有隙，突厥入朝，請雄及其妻子，將甘心焉。

translations.literal: Xiong first had a grudge with the Turks; when the Turks came to court they requested Xiong and his wife and children, intending to take their hearts' satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong had earlier quarreled with the Turks; when a Turkish envoy came to court, he demanded Xiong and his family to settle the feud.

sentences.zh: 周遂遣之。

translations.literal: Zhou thereupon sent them.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou agreed to hand them over.

sentences.zh: 威曰：「夷人昧利，可以賂動。

translations.literal: Wei said: "Barbarians do not understand profit and can be moved by bribes."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Barbarians care only for gain and can be bought off."

sentences.zh: 」遂標賣田宅，罄家所有以贖雄，論者義之。

translations.literal: He thereupon posted notices selling fields and houses, exhausted all the family possessed to redeem Xiong; opinion holders praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He sold his lands and property, gave all he had to ransom Xiong, and won universal praise for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，就拜開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he was appointed at his post as General with independent command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he accepted appointment as a general with an independent command.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，高熲屢言其賢，高祖亦素重其名，召之。

translations.literal: When the Founder was Chancellor, Gao Jiong repeatedly spoke of his worth; the Founder also from of old esteemed his name and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chief minister, Gao Jiong repeatedly praised his talent, and Yang Jian, who had long respected his reputation, summoned him.

sentences.zh: 及至，引入臥內，與語大悅。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was led into the sleeping quarters; on speaking together they were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival he was received in the prince's private quarters; their conversation delighted them both.

sentences.zh: 居月余，威聞禪代之議，遁歸田裡。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Wei heard talk of the abdication and transfer of the Mandate, and fled back to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he heard talk of usurpation and fled home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 高熲請追之，高祖曰：「此不欲預吾事，且置之。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong requested to pursue him; the Founder said: "This man does not wish to take part in my affairs — for the time being let him be."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong urged that he be brought back, but Yang Jian said, "He does not wish to be part of my enterprise — leave him be for now."

sentences.zh: 」及受禪，征拜太子少保。

translations.literal: "When he received the abdication, he was summoned and appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication he was summoned and made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 追贈其父為邳國公，邑三千戶，以威襲焉。

translations.literal: His father was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Pi State with a fief of three thousand households; Wei inherited it.
translations.idiomatic: His father was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Pi with three thousand households, and Wei succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 俄兼納言、民部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally Censor-in-Chief and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made censor-in-chief and minister of revenue as well.

sentences.zh: 威上表陳讓，詔曰：「舟大者任重，馬駿者遠馳。

translations.literal: Wei submitted a memorial declining; an edict said: "A great boat bears heavy cargo; a swift horse runs far."
translations.idiomatic: Wei memorialized to decline; the edict read, "A great vessel bears heavy cargo; a swift horse runs far."

sentences.zh: 以公有兼人之才，無辭多務也。

translations.literal: "Because you, sir, have talent to match several men, do not decline many affairs."
translations.idiomatic: "You have the capacity of several men — do not shirk heavy duties."

sentences.zh: 」威乃止。

translations.literal: "Wei thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wei thereupon accepted.

sentences.zh: 初，威父在西魏，以國用不足，為徵稅之法，頗稱為重。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Wei's father in Western Wei, because state revenue was insufficient, made a method of levying taxes, which was rather called heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei's father in Western Wei, facing insufficient revenue, had devised a tax system widely regarded as harsh.

sentences.zh: 既而歎曰：「今所為者，正如張弓，非平世法也。

translations.literal: Afterward he sighed and said: "What is now being done is just like drawing a bow — it is not the law of a peaceful age."
translations.idiomatic: He later sighed and said, "What I have done is like drawing a bow taut — it is no law for times of peace."

sentences.zh: 後之君子，誰能弛乎？

translations.literal: "Later gentlemen — who will be able to relax it?"
translations.idiomatic: "Which of the gentlemen to come will be able to loosen the string?"

sentences.zh: 」威聞其言，每以為己任。

translations.literal: "Wei heard his words and always took them as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took these words as his personal mission.

sentences.zh: 至是，奏減賦役，務從輕典，上悉從之。

translations.literal: At this time he memorialized to reduce taxes and corvée, striving to follow light statutes; the sovereign entirely followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Now he memorialized to lighten taxes and labor service, and the emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 漸見親重，與高熲參掌朝政。

translations.literal: He gradually was seen as intimate and weighty, and with Gao Jiong jointly managed court administration.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually won the emperor's trust and shared governance with Gao Jiong.

sentences.zh: 威見宮中以銀為幔鉤，因盛陳節儉之美以諭上。

translations.literal: Wei saw in the palace that silver was used for curtain hooks, and thereupon fully set forth the beauty of frugality to instruct the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing silver curtain hooks in the palace, he lectured the emperor at length on the virtues of frugality.

sentences.zh: 上為之改容，雕飾舊物，悉命除毀。

translations.literal: The sovereign because of this changed expression; carved and decorated old objects were all ordered removed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his point; all ornamental luxuries in the palace were ordered destroyed.

sentences.zh: 上嘗怒一人，將殺之，威入閤進諫，不納。

translations.literal: The sovereign once in anger wished to kill a man; Wei entered the gate and advanced remonstrance, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in anger, the emperor was about to execute a man; Wei entered and remonstrated, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 上怒甚，將自出斬之，威當上前不去。

translations.literal: The sovereign was very angry and was about to go out himself and behead him; Wei blocked before him and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, furious, rose to kill the man himself; Wei barred his way and would not budge.

sentences.zh: 上避之而出，威又遮止。

translations.literal: The sovereign avoided him and went out; Wei again obstructed and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried to go around him; Wei blocked him again.

sentences.zh: 上拂衣而入。

translations.literal: The sovereign brushed his robes and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brushed past him and withdrew inside.

sentences.zh: 良久，乃召威謝曰：「公能若是，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: After a long while he then summoned Wei and apologized, saying: "You, sir, can be like this — I have no worries."
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he summoned Wei and said, "If you will be thus steadfast, I have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」於是賜馬二匹，錢十余萬。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he gave two horses and more than a hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with two horses and more than a hundred thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 尋複兼大理卿、京兆尹、御史大夫，本官悉如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was again concurrently Minister of Justice, Jingzhao Intendant, and Censor-in-Chief; his original offices all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent posts as minister of justice, intendant of Jingzhao, and censor-in-chief, while retaining his existing offices.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史梁毗以威領五職，安繁戀劇，無舉賢自代之心，抗表劾威。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liang Pi, because Wei held five offices, was content with complexity and clung to busy affairs, and had no mind to recommend the worthy to replace himself, submitted a memorial impeaching Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Liang Pi impeached him for holding five offices at once, clinging to power, and failing to recommend a successor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「蘇威朝夕孜孜，志存遠大，舉賢有闕，何遽迫之！

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Su Wei morning and evening is diligent and earnest, his aim set on the far-reaching; in recommending the worthy he has shortcomings — why press him so urgently!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Su Wei works tirelessly and thinks only of the public good; if he has been slow to promote others, why hound him?"

sentences.zh: 」顧謂威曰：「用之則行，舍之則藏，唯我與爾有是夫！

translations.literal: "He turned to Wei and said: "Employed, then he acts; released, then he hides — only you and I have this!"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Wei and said, "In office one serves; out of office one withdraws — only you and I understand this!"

sentences.zh: 」因謂朝臣曰：「蘇威不值我，無以措其言；

translations.literal: He thereupon said to the court ministers: "If Su Wei did not meet with me, he would have nowhere to set forth his words;
translations.idiomatic: He told the court, "Without me, Su Wei would have no one to hear him;

sentences.zh: 我不得蘇威，何以行其道？

translations.literal: if I did not obtain Su Wei, how could I carry out the Way?"
translations.idiomatic: without Su Wei, how could I put my principles into practice?"

sentences.zh: 楊素才辯無雙，至若斟酌古今，助我宣化，非威之匹也。

translations.literal: Yang Su's talent and eloquence are without peer, but as for weighing past and present to aid me in spreading transformation — he is not Su Wei's match.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su is unrivaled in wit, but when it comes to weighing past and present to help me govern, he is no match for Su Wei.

sentences.zh: 蘇威若逢亂世，南山四皓，豈易屈哉！

translations.literal: Su Wei, if he met a chaotic age, would be like the Four Hoaryheads of the Southern Mountains — how easily could he be bent!
translations.idiomatic: In a time of chaos, Su Wei would be like the Four Whiteheads of Mount Shang — not easily bent from his course!

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree to which he was esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜刑部尚書，解少保、御史大夫之官。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Justice and relieved of the offices of Junior Guardian and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of justice and relieved of his posts as junior guardian and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 後京兆尹廢，檢校雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Later the Jingzhao Intendant post was abolished; he was made Acting Vice Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Jingzhao intendant was abolished, he was named acting vice governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 時高熲與威同心協贊，政刑大小，無不籌之，故革運數年，天下稱治。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Jiong and Wei were of one heart in mutual support; in government and punishments, great and small, nothing was not planned by them, and therefore within several years of the change of mandate all under Heaven praised good order.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and Wei worked in concert; nothing of policy or law passed without their counsel, and within a few years the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 俄轉民部尚書，納言如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Minister of Revenue, Censor-in-Chief as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to minister of revenue while retaining the post of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 屬山東諸州民饑，上令威賑恤之。

translations.literal: It happened that in the eastern mountain provinces the people suffered famine; the sovereign ordered Wei to relieve and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the eastern provinces, the emperor sent Wei to organize relief.

sentences.zh: 後二載，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After two years he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，兼領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he additionally headed the Directorate of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A year afterward he was also made director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 隋承戰爭之後，憲章踳駁，上令朝臣厘改舊法，為一代通典。

translations.literal: Sui inherited after warfare; statutes and regulations were confused and contradictory; the sovereign ordered court ministers to revise the old laws and make a comprehensive code for the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui inherited a realm shattered by war, with laws in disarray; the emperor ordered the court to codify a new legal system for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 律令格式，多威所定，世以為能。

translations.literal: Statutes, ordinances, formats, and styles — many were set by Wei; the age considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the new code of statutes, ordinances, and formats was Wei's work, and contemporaries judged him master of it.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其年，以母憂去職，柴毀骨立。

translations.literal: That year, on his mother's mourning he left office; his mourning destruction left him skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: That year he left office to mourn his mother and was reduced to skin and bone by grief.

sentences.zh: 上敕威曰：「公德行高人，情寄殊重，大孝之道，蓋同俯就。

translations.literal: The sovereign charged Wei: "Your virtue and conduct are lofty, and my personal regard for you is especially weighty; in the way of great filial piety, one should likewise bend to comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urged him, "Your virtue is eminent and my reliance on you is great; even in deepest mourning you must bend to necessity.

sentences.zh: 必須抑割，為國惜身。

translations.literal: You must restrain and cut short, cherishing your person for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Restrain your grief and preserve yourself for the state.

sentences.zh: 朕之於公，為君為父，宜依朕旨，以禮自存。

translations.literal: I toward you am both sovereign and father; you should follow my intent and preserve yourself by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I stand to you as both sovereign and father; heed my command and observe proper measure."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，起令視事，固辭，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to attend to business; he firmly declined, but an excellent edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered back to duty; he protested, but a gracious edict would not allow refusal.

sentences.zh: 明年，上幸并州，命與高熲同總留事。

translations.literal: The next year the sovereign visited Bingzhou and ordered him together with Gao Jiong jointly to oversee remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the emperor visited Bingzhou, he and Gao Jiong were left jointly in charge of the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄追詣行在所，使決民訟。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the traveling palace and made to decide the people's lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the emperor's camp to adjudicate civil suits.

sentences.zh: 威子夔，少有盛名於天下，引致賓客，四海士大夫多歸之。

translations.literal: Wei's son Kui from youth had great fame under Heaven, drew in guests, and scholars and officials of the four seas mostly attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son Kui enjoyed wide renown from youth, gathered guests, and drew scholars from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 後議樂事，夔與國子博士何妥各有所持。

translations.literal: Later when music matters were discussed, Kui and the National University academician He Tuo each held their own positions.
translations.idiomatic: When court debated ritual music, Kui and the academician He Tuo took opposing positions.

sentences.zh: 於是夔、妥俱為一議，使百僚署其所同。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kui and Tuo each made one proposal and had the hundred officials sign which they agreed with.
translations.idiomatic: Each drafted a proposal and had the officials sign in support of one side or the other.

sentences.zh: 朝廷多附威，同夔者十八九。

translations.literal: The court mostly attached to Wei; those agreeing with Kui were eight or nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the court sided with Wei; eight or nine tenths of the officials backed Kui.

sentences.zh: 妥恚曰：「吾席間函丈四十餘年，反為昨暮兒之所屈也！

translations.literal: Tuo in anger said: "I have lectured at my mat for more than forty years, and in the end am bent by a lad of yesterday evening!"
translations.idiomatic: He Tuo fumed, "I have taught from this chair for forty years, only to be overruled by some upstart!"

sentences.zh: 」遂奏威與禮部尚書盧愷、吏部侍郎薛道衡、尚書右丞王弘、考功侍郎李同和等共為朋黨，省中呼王弘為世子，李同和為叔，言二人如威之子弟也。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized that Wei together with Minister of Rites Lu Kai, Vice Director of Personnel Xue Daoheng, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong, and Review Section Vice Director Li Tonghe and others jointly formed a faction; within the ministry they called Wang Hong the heir apparent and Li Tonghe the uncle, saying the two were like Wei's sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Wei, Lu Kai, Xue Daoheng, Wang Hong, Li Tonghe, and others had formed a faction; in the ministry Wang Hong was called "the heir" and Li Tonghe "the uncle," as though they were Wei's kin.

sentences.zh: 複言威以曲道任其從父弟徹、肅等罔冒為官。

translations.literal: He again said Wei by crooked paths had his cousin younger brothers Che and Su and others falsely registered and appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: He also charged that Wei had used improper influence to secure offices for his cousins Che and Su.

sentences.zh: 又國子學請蕩陰人王孝逸為書學博士，威屬盧愷，以為其府參軍。

translations.literal: Moreover the Imperial Academy requested Wang Xiaoyi of Dangyin as Doctor of Calligraphy; Wei through Lu Kai had him made a staff officer in his own bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the academy sought Wang Xiaoyi as calligraphy instructor, Wei had Lu Kai appoint him to his own staff instead.

sentences.zh: 上令蜀王秀、上柱國虞慶則等雜治之，事皆驗。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Prince of Shu Xiu, Supreme Pillar of State Yu Qingze, and others jointly to investigate; the matters were all verified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince Xiu of Shu, Yu Qingze, and others to investigate; every charge was substantiated.

sentences.zh: 上以《宋書·謝晦傳》中朋黨事令威讀之。

translations.literal: The sovereign had Wei read the faction affair in the "Biography of Xie Hui" in the History of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Wei read the account of factionalism in Xie Hui's biography in the History of Song.

sentences.zh: 威惶懼，免冠頓首。

translations.literal: Wei in fear and trembling removed his cap and knocked his head on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wei prostrated himself in terror.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「謝已晚矣。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "To apologize is already late."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your apology comes too late."

sentences.zh: 」於是免威官爵，以開府就第。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wei was dismissed from office and rank and as General with independent command returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was stripped of office and rank but allowed to keep his noble status and retire home.

sentences.zh: 知名之士坐威得罪者百餘人。

translations.literal: Notable scholars who sat with Wei and were punished numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred prominent men who had associated with him were punished as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上曰：「蘇威德行者，但為人所誤耳。

translations.literal: Before long the sovereign said: "Su Wei is a man of virtue — he was only misled by others."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor said, "Su Wei is a man of integrity who was led astray by others."

sentences.zh: 」命之通籍。

translations.literal: He ordered him registered for court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to resume attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，複爵邳公，拜納言。

translations.literal: After more than a year his title Duke of Pi was restored and he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: A year later his dukedom of Pi was restored and he was again made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從祠太山，坐不敬免。

translations.literal: Following the emperor in sacrificing at Mount Tai, he sat improperly and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On the Mount Tai sacrifice he was dismissed for an impropriety in ritual deportment.

sentences.zh: 俄而復位。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reinstated.

sentences.zh: 上謂群臣曰：「世人言蘇威詐清，家累金玉，此妄言也。

translations.literal: The sovereign said to the assembled ministers: "Men say Su Wei feigns purity while his house is piled with gold and jade — this is false talk."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers, "People call Su Wei a hypocrite who hoards gold and jade — that is slander."

sentences.zh: 然其性狠戾，不切世要，求名太甚，從己則悅，違之必怒，此其大病耳。

translations.literal: "Yet his nature is harsh and perverse, not cutting to the needs of the age; he seeks fame too greatly; if one follows him he is pleased, if one opposes him he is certain to rage — this is his great fault."
translations.idiomatic: "But he is harsh and obstinate, out of touch with the times, and too eager for reputation; flatter him and he is pleased, cross him and he flies into a rage — that is his grave flaw."

sentences.zh: 」尋令持節巡撫江南，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to hold the staff of authority and tour and pacify the south, with power to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent with imperial authority to tour and pacify the south, empowered to act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 過會稽，逾五嶺而還。

translations.literal: Passing Kuaiji, he crossed the Five Ridges and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through Kuaiji, crossed the Five Ridges, and returned.

sentences.zh: 時突厥都藍可汗屢為邊患，複使威至可汗所，與結和親。

translations.literal: At the time Tulan Qaghan of the Turks repeatedly caused border trouble; Wei was again sent to the qaghan's place to form a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Tulan Qaghan raided the frontier, Wei was again sent to negotiate a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 可汗即遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: The qaghan thereupon sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 以勤勞，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: For diligent labor he was advanced to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: For his exertions he was promoted to great general.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，複拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was again appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Renshou era he was again named right vice director.

sentences.zh: 上幸仁壽宮，以威總留後事。

translations.literal: The sovereign visited Renshou Palace and had Wei oversee remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Renshou Palace, Wei was left in charge of the capital.

sentences.zh: 及上還，御史奏威職事多不理，請推之。

translations.literal: When the sovereign returned, the censor memorialized that Wei in his duties mostly did not manage well and requested investigation.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return, censors reported that Wei had neglected his duties and asked for an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 上怒，詰責威。

translations.literal: The sovereign was angry and interrogated and reproached Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 威拜謝，上亦止。

translations.literal: Wei bowed in apology; the sovereign also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wei kowtowed in apology, and the emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 後上幸仁壽宮，不豫，皇太子自京師來侍疾，詔威留守京師。

translations.literal: Later the sovereign visited Renshou Palace and was unwell; the crown prince came from the capital to attend the illness; an edict ordered Wei to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, the crown prince came from the capital to attend him, and Wei was ordered to remain in charge at the capital.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，加上大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was additionally made Supreme General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was further promoted to supreme general.

sentences.zh: 及長城之役，威諫止之。

translations.literal: When the Great Wall labor was launched, Wei remonstrated to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Wall project began, Wei remonstrated against it.

sentences.zh: 高熲、賀若弼等之誅也，威坐與相連，免官。

translations.literal: At the executions of Gao Jiong, He Ruo Bi, and others, Wei sat in connection with them and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jiong and He Ruo Bi were executed, Wei was implicated and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜魯郡太守。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Governor of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed governor of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 俄召還，參預朝政。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled and participated in court administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to take part in government again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜太常卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 其年從征吐谷渾，進位左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That year he followed the campaign against Tuyuhun and was advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: That year he accompanied the campaign against Tuyuhun and was promoted to left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 帝以威先朝舊臣，漸加委任。

translations.literal: The sovereign, because Wei was an old minister of the previous reign, gradually added to his commission.
translations.idiomatic: As a veteran of the previous reign, he was gradually entrusted with greater authority.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，複為納言。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was again made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 與左翊衛大將軍宇文述、黃門侍郎裴矩、御史大夫裴蘊、內史侍郎虞世基參掌朝政，時人稱為「五貴」。

translations.literal: Together with Left Guard General-in-Chief Yuwen Shu, Yellow Gate Vice Director Pei Ju, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, and Palace Secretariat Vice Director Yu Shiji he jointly managed court administration; men of the time called them the "Five Exalted."
translations.idiomatic: He shared power with Yuwen Shu, Pei Ju, Pei Yun, and Yu Shiji — the "Five Exalted" of the age.

sentences.zh: 及遼東之役，以本官領左武衛大將軍，進位光祿大夫，賜爵甯陵侯。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong campaign was launched, in his original office he headed the Left Martial Guard General-in-Chief, was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and enfeoffed Marquis of Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he commanded the Left Martial Guard, was made grand master of splendid happiness, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningling.

sentences.zh: 其年，進封房公。

translations.literal: That year he was advanced to Duke of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was advanced to Duke of Fang.

sentences.zh: 威以年老，上表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Wei because of old age submitted a memorial begging to retire on broken bones.
