translations.idiomatic: Citing old age, he memorialized to retire.

sentences.zh: 上不許，複以本官參掌選事。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not permit it and again had him in his original office participate in and manage selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and kept him in charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 明年，從征遼東，領右禦衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the Liaodong campaign and headed the Right Imperial Guard General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he accompanied the Liaodong campaign as general of the Right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之反也，帝引威帳中，懼見於色，謂威曰：「此小兒聰明，得不為患乎？

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the sovereign drew Wei into his tent, fear showing on his face, and said to Wei: "This lad is clever — could he not become a trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor summoned Wei to his tent, fear plain on his face, and asked, "The boy is clever — might he not prove dangerous?"

sentences.zh: 」威曰：「夫識是非，審成敗者，乃所謂聰明。

translations.literal: Wei said: "He who knows right and wrong and judges success and failure — that is what is called clever."
translations.idiomatic: Wei replied, "True cleverness is knowing right from wrong and success from failure.

sentences.zh: 玄感粗疏，非聰明者，必無所慮。

translations.literal: Xuangan is coarse and careless; he is not a clever man and will certainly not be a source of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan is crude and rash — not clever at all — and need not trouble you.

sentences.zh: 但恐浸成亂階耳。

translations.literal: "I only fear he will gradually become a source of disorder."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear he may open the way to wider rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」威見勞役不息，百姓思亂，微以此諷帝，帝竟不寤。

translations.literal: Wei saw that corvée labor did not cease and the common people longed for disorder; he subtly used this to admonish the sovereign, but the sovereign in the end did not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing endless labor and growing popular unrest, Wei hinted at his concern, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 從還至涿郡，詔威安撫關中。

translations.literal: On returning from the campaign to Zhuo Commandery, an edict ordered Wei to pacify Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Zhuo Commandery he was ordered to pacify Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 以威孫尚輦直長儇為副。

translations.literal: Wei's grandson Xuan, Direct Attendant of the Imperial Carriage, was made his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xuan, an attendant of the imperial carriage, was named his deputy.

sentences.zh: 其子鴻臚少卿夔，先為關中簡黜大使，一家三人，俱奉使關右，三輔榮之。

translations.literal: His son Kui, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, had first been Grand Selection and Dismissal Commissioner for Guanzhong — one family, three men, all on mission in the right of Guan; the three metropolitan districts were honored by it.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui had already served as selection commissioner for Guanzhong — three members of one family on mission in the west, to the capital's glory.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，帝下手詔曰：「玉以潔潤，丹紫莫能渝其質；

translations.literal: After more than a year the sovereign personally wrote an edict, saying: "Jade through purity and moistness — cinnabar and purple cannot change its substance;
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the emperor wrote, "Jade is pure and cannot be stained;

sentences.zh: 松表歲寒，霜雪莫能凋其采。

translations.literal: the pine shows the year's cold; frost and snow cannot wither its splendor.
translations.idiomatic: the pine stays green in winter — frost and snow cannot kill it.

sentences.zh: 可謂溫仁勁直，性之然乎！

translations.literal: One may call this warm benevolence and firm uprightness — such is the nature!"
translations.idiomatic: Such are warmth, benevolence, and steadfast integrity."

sentences.zh: 房公威器懷溫裕，識量弘雅，早居端揆，備悉國章，先皇舊臣，朝之宿齒。

translations.literal: Duke of Fang Wei's capacity embraces warmth and abundance, his discernment and measure are broad and elegant; early he occupied the pinnacle of state, fully knowing the state's regulations; an old minister of the former emperor, a senior tooth of the court.
translations.idiomatic: "Duke of Fang Wei is temperate and magnanimous, learned in statecraft, an elder statesman of the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 棟樑社稷，弼諧朕躬，守文奉法，卑身率禮。

translations.literal: Pillar and beam of the altars of soil and grain, he harmonizes and aids my person, keeps the laws and follows statutes, lowers his person and leads in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He is a pillar of the realm who assists my rule, keeps the laws, and models propriety.

sentences.zh: 昔漢之三傑，輔惠帝者蕭何；

translations.literal: Of old in Han's three outstanding men, the one who assisted Emperor Hui was Xiao He;
translations.idiomatic: Of Han's three heroes, Xiao He steadied the reign of Emperor Hui;

sentences.zh: 周之十亂，佐成王者邵奭。

translations.literal: of Zhou's ten chaotic elements, the one who assisted the completing king was Shao Shi.
translations.idiomatic: of the ten sage ministers of Zhou, the Duke of Shao aided King Cheng.

sentences.zh: 國之寶器，其在得賢，參燮臺階，具瞻斯允。

translations.literal: The state's precious vessel lies in obtaining the worthy; harmonizing the terrace steps — all look to this as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: A state's treasure is worthy men; he harmonizes the government and commands universal trust.

sentences.zh: 雖複事藉論道，終期獻替，銓衡時務，朝寄為重，可開府儀同三司，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Although affairs rely on discourse of the Way, in the end the expectation is to offer replacements; balancing the times' affairs — the court's commission is weighty — he may be General Equal in Three Ranks, all else as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be made general equal in three ranks; all other honors remain."

sentences.zh: 」威當時見尊重，朝臣莫與為比。

translations.literal: Wei at the time was seen as respected; no court minister could be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time no minister stood higher in honor.

sentences.zh: 後從幸雁門，為突厥所圍，朝廷危憚。

translations.literal: Later he followed in attending at Yanmen and was surrounded by the Turks; the court was gravely fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Yanmen, the court was surrounded by Turks and thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 帝欲輕騎潰圍而出，威諫曰：「城守則我有餘力，輕騎則彼之所長。

translations.literal: The sovereign wished to break out with light cavalry; Wei remonstrated: "In defending a city our strength is more than sufficient; in light cavalry that is their strong point.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to break out with a light cavalry escort. Wei objected, "We are strong in defense; they excel at mounted raiding.

sentences.zh: 陛下萬乘之主，何宜輕脫！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is master of the ten thousand chariots — how is it fitting to slip away lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is the Son of Heaven — you must not risk yourself so lightly!"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held his position.

sentences.zh: 突厥俄亦解圍而去。

translations.literal: The Turks before long also lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks soon lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 車駕至太原，威言於帝曰：「今者盜賊不止，士馬疲敝。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Taiyuan; Wei spoke to the sovereign, saying: "Now bandits and robbers do not stop; soldiers and horses are weary and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan, Wei told the emperor, "Rebels are everywhere and the army is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 願陛下還京師，深根固本，為社稷之計。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to return to the capital, deeply root and solidify the foundation, for the altars of soil and grain's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Return to the capital, strengthen your foundations, and think of the dynasty's survival."

sentences.zh: 」帝初然之，竟用宇文述等議，遂往東都。

translations.literal: The sovereign at first agreed, but in the end followed Yuwen Shu and others' plan and thereupon went to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first agreed, but Yuwen Shu and his faction prevailed, and the court proceeded to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時天下大亂，威知帝不可改，意甚患之。

translations.literal: At the time all under Heaven was in great disorder; Wei knew the sovereign could not be changed and was greatly grieved in mind.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire collapsing, Wei knew the emperor would not change course, and he was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 屬帝問侍臣盜賊事，宇文述曰：「盜賊信少，不足為虞。

translations.literal: It happened that the sovereign asked attending ministers about bandit affairs; Yuwen Shu said: "Bandits are truly few — not enough to cause concern."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked his attendants about rebels, Yuwen Shu said, "They are few and hardly worth concern."

sentences.zh: 」威不能詭對，以身隱於殿柱。

translations.literal: Wei could not answer deceitfully and hid his person behind a hall pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Wei could not bring himself to lie and slipped behind a pillar.

sentences.zh: 帝呼威而問之。

translations.literal: The sovereign called Wei and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called him forth and pressed him for an answer.

sentences.zh: 威對曰：「臣非職司，不知多少，但患其漸近。

translations.literal: Wei replied: "Your servant is not in that office and does not know the number; he only fears they are drawing gradually near."
translations.idiomatic: Wei answered, "I am not in charge of such reports and do not know the count — I only fear they are drawing nearer every day."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What do you mean by that?"

sentences.zh: 」威曰：「他日賊據長白山，今者近在滎陽、汜水。

translations.literal: Wei said: "In other days bandits held Changbai Mountain; now they are close at Xingyang and Sishui."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Once the rebels held distant Changbai; now they are at Xingyang and Sishui, on our doorstep."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅而罷。

translations.literal: The sovereign was displeased and dismissed the session.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and cut the audience short.

sentences.zh: 尋屬五月五日，百僚上饋，多以珍玩。

translations.literal: Before long it was the fifth day of the fifth month; the hundred officials presented gifts, mostly rare curios.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month the officials presented gifts, mostly luxuries.

sentences.zh: 威獻《尚書》一部，微以諷帝，帝彌不平。

translations.literal: Wei presented one copy of the Documents and subtly used it to admonish the sovereign; the sovereign grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wei offered a copy of the Book of Documents as his gift — a pointed rebuke — which angered the emperor all the more.

sentences.zh: 後複問伐遼東事，威對願赦群盜，遣討高麗，帝益怒。

translations.literal: Later when the Liaodong campaign was again discussed, Wei replied that he wished to pardon the bandits in mass and send them to attack Goryeo; the sovereign grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liaodong campaign came up again, Wei proposed pardoning the rebels and sending them against Goryeo instead; the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫裴蘊希旨，令白衣張行本奏威昔在高陽典選，濫授人官，畏怯突厥，請還京師。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun to please the sovereign's intent ordered the commoner Zhang Xingben to memorialize that Wei in the past at Gaoyang managed selection, wantonly granted men office, feared the Turks, and requested return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yun, eager to please, had Zhang Xingben accuse Wei of abusing appointments while selecting officials at Gaoyang and of cowardice before the Turks.

sentences.zh: 帝令案其事。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered the matter investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 及獄成，下詔曰：「威立性朋黨，好為異端，懷挾詭道，徼幸名利，詆訶律令，謗訕台省。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, an edict was issued, saying: "Wei by nature forms factions, delights in heterodox ways, harbors crooked doctrines, schemes for reputation and profit, slanders statutes and ordinances, and mocks the ministries."
translations.idiomatic: When the case closed, the edict condemned Wei for factionalism, heterodoxy, slander of the laws, and contempt for the ministries.

sentences.zh: 昔歲薄伐，奉述先志，凡預切問，各盡胸臆，而威不以開懷，遂無對命。

translations.literal: "In last year's shallow campaign we followed and expounded the former intent; all who received direct inquiry each exhausted their breast and thoughts, yet Wei did not thereby open his heart and accordingly had no reply to the command."
translations.idiomatic: "At last year's campaign every minister spoke his mind, yet Wei would not speak frankly to the throne."

sentences.zh: 啟沃之道，其若是乎！

translations.literal: "The way of opening and moistening — is it like this!"
translations.idiomatic: "Is this how a minister should counsel his sovereign?"

sentences.zh: 資敬之義，何其甚薄！

translations.literal: "The meaning of cherishing respect — how very thin!"
translations.idiomatic: "Where is the respect owed to the throne?"

sentences.zh: 」於是除名為民。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he was stripped of name and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of rank and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，有人奏威與突厥陰圖不軌者，大理簿責威。

translations.literal: After more than a month someone memorialized that Wei with the Turks secretly plotted sedition; the Court of Judicial Review interrogated Wei.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was accused of plotting with the Turks; the judiciary interrogated him.

sentences.zh: 威自陳奉事二朝三十余載，精誠微淺不能上感，咎釁屢彰，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: Wei himself stated that he had served two reigns for more than thirty years; his sincerity was slight and could not move above, his faults and omens repeatedly appeared, and his crime deserved ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Wei confessed that he had served two emperors for thirty years without earning their trust, had erred repeatedly, and deserved death ten thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 帝憫而釋之。

translations.literal: The sovereign pitied him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity and released him.

sentences.zh: 其年從幸江都宮，帝將複用威。

translations.literal: That year he followed in attending at Jiangdu Palace; the sovereign was about to employ Wei again.
translations.idiomatic: That year, at Jiangdu, the emperor was about to restore him to office.

sentences.zh: 裴蘊、虞世基奏言昏耄贏疾。

translations.literal: Pei Yun and Yu Shiji memorialized that he was senile, decrepit, and ill.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yun and Yu Shiji reported that he was senile and infirm.

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆也，以威為光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he made Wei Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and General Equal in Three Ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, he appointed Wei grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，歸於李密。

translations.literal: When Huaji was defeated, he went over to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji's defeat he joined Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 未幾密敗，歸東都，越王侗以為上柱國、邳公。

translations.literal: Before long Mi was defeated; he returned to the Eastern Capital, and the Prince of Yue Tong made him Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi fell, he went to the Eastern Capital, where Prince Yue Tong made him supreme pillar of state and Duke of Pi.

sentences.zh: 王充僭號，署太師。

translations.literal: Wang Chong usurped the title and appointed him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong declared himself emperor and named him grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 威自以隋室舊臣，遭逢喪亂，所經之處，皆與時消息，以求容免。

translations.literal: Wei considered himself an old minister of the Sui house, encountering repeated turmoil; wherever he passed he all followed the times' messages, seeking to obtain tolerance and escape.
translations.idiomatic: As a Sui veteran adrift in civil war, he adapted to each new master in order to survive.

sentences.zh: 及大唐秦王平王充，坐於東都閶闔門內，威請謁見，稱老病不能拜起。

translations.literal: When the Great Tang Prince of Qin pacified Wang Chong, sitting inside the Chongle Gate of the Eastern Capital, Wei requested an audience, saying he was old and ill and could not bow and rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang Prince of Qin took Luoyang, Wei asked to see him, pleading age and infirmity.

sentences.zh: 王遣人數之曰：「公隋朝宰輔，政亂不能匡救，遂令品物塗炭，君弑國亡。

translations.literal: The prince sent someone to reproach him, saying: "You, sir, were chief minister of the Sui dynasty; when government was chaotic you could not rescue and correct it, and thus caused all things to be smeared with charcoal, the ruler murdered and the state perished."
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent word: "As Sui chief minister you failed to save the dynasty from ruin and the emperor from murder."

sentences.zh: 見李密、王充，皆拜伏舞蹈。

translations.literal: "Seeing Li Mi and Wang Chong, you all bowed prostrate and danced."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet you bowed and scraped before Li Mi and Wang Chong."

sentences.zh: 今既老病，無勞相見也。

translations.literal: "Now that you are old and ill, there is no need to meet."
translations.idiomatic: "Now that you are old and sick, there is no need to meet."

sentences.zh: 」尋歸長安，至朝堂請見，又不許。

translations.literal: "Before long he returned to Chang'an; reaching the audience hall he requested audience, and again was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Chang'an and was refused audience at the palace.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 時年八十二。

translations.literal: At the time his age was eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 威治身清儉，以廉慎見稱。

translations.literal: Wei in governing his person was pure and frugal, and was praised for integrity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Wei lived plainly and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 每至公議，惡人異己，雖或小事，必固爭之。

translations.literal: Whenever public discussion arose, he hated men differing from him; even if a small matter, he must stubbornly dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: In council he could not abide disagreement and would argue stubbornly over trifles.

sentences.zh: 時人以為無大臣之體。

translations.literal: Men of the time thought he lacked the substance of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries judged him wanting in the magnanimity of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 所修格令章程，並行於當世，然頗傷苛碎，論者以為非簡允之法。

translations.literal: The regulations, formats, and statutes he revised all were practiced in his age, yet they rather wounded through severity and minuteness; opinion holders considered them not the method of simplicity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The codes he drafted governed the age but were criticized as excessively harsh and minute.

sentences.zh: 及大業末年，尤多征役，至於論功行賞，威每承望風旨，輒寢其事。

translations.literal: By the end of the Daye era corvée especially multiplied; as for discussing merit and carrying out rewards, Wei often received and followed the wind of the sovereign's intent and then shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Daye years, when merit rewards were due, Wei often bowed to the emperor's mood and let them lapse.

sentences.zh: 時群盜蜂起，郡縣有表奏詣闕者，又訶詰使人，令減賊數。

translations.literal: At the time bandits swarmed like bees; commanderies and counties had memorials and reports reaching the palace, yet he again interrogated and reproached the envoys, ordering them to reduce the bandit count.
translations.idiomatic: As rebels multiplied, he bullied local officials into understating rebel numbers in their reports.

sentences.zh: 故出師攻討，多不克捷。

translations.literal: Therefore when armies went out to attack and punish, many did not achieve victory.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial campaigns therefore often failed.

sentences.zh: 由是為物議所譏。

translations.literal: Thereby he was ridiculed in public discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 子夔。

translations.literal: His son Kui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui.

sentences.zh: 子夔夔字伯尼，少聰敏，有口辯。

translations.literal: His son Kui — Kui styled Bonai — from youth was clever and keen, with eloquence in speech.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui, styled Bonai, was clever and eloquent from childhood.

sentences.zh: 八歲誦詩書，兼解騎射。

translations.literal: At eight he recited the Book of Songs and Documents, and also understood riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he was reciting the classics and had learned riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 年十三，從父至尚書省，與安德王雄馳射，賭得雄駿馬而歸。

translations.literal: At thirteen he followed his father to the Department of State Affairs and with Prince of Ande Xiong competed in mounted archery, gambling and winning Xiong's fine horse and returning.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he accompanied his father to the Secretariat and won a fine horse from Prince Xiong of Ande in an archery wager.

sentences.zh: 十四詣學，與諸儒論議，詞致可觀，見者莫不稱善。

translations.literal: At fourteen he went to the academy and with the various Confucians debated; his rhetoric was worth viewing, and those who saw him none did not praise his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he debated the Confucian scholars at the academy and impressed all who heard him.

sentences.zh: 及長，博覽群言，尤以鐘律自命。

translations.literal: When grown, he broadly perused many teachings and especially took bells and pitch pipes as his calling.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he read widely and styled himself an authority on music and pitch.

sentences.zh: 初不名夔，其父改之，頗為有識所哂。

translations.literal: At first he was not named Kui; his father changed it, and this was rather ridiculed by those with understanding.
translations.idiomatic: His father had renamed him Kui, to the amusement of knowing observers.

sentences.zh: 起家太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant Gentleman of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He began as attendant gentleman to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 楊素甚奇之，素每戲威曰：「楊素無兒，蘇夔無父。

translations.literal: Yang Su greatly marveled at him; Su often jested with Wei, saying: "Yang Su has no son; Su Kui has no father."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su greatly admired him and jested to Su Wei, "Yang Su has no son; Su Kui has no father."

sentences.zh: 」後與沛國公鄭譯、國子博士何妥議樂，因而得罪，議寢不行。

translations.literal: "Later with Duke of Pei State Zheng Yi and National University academician He Tuo he debated music, and thereby offended; the debate was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He later clashed with Zheng Yi and He Tuo over music reform and fell from favor; his proposals were shelved.

sentences.zh: 著《樂志》十五篇，以見其志。

translations.literal: He composed fifteen chapters of "Treatise on Music" to show his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote fifteen chapters of a Treatise on Music to set forth his views.

sentences.zh: 數載，遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: After several years he was promoted to Secretary of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was promoted to secretary of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 後加武騎尉。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally made Martial Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made martial cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，詔天下舉達禮樂之源者，晉王昭時為雍州牧，舉夔應之。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou an edict ordered all under Heaven to recommend those who had mastered the sources of ritual and music; Prince of Jin Zhao at the time was Governor of Yong Province and recommended Kui in response.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Renshou the throne sought experts in ritual music; Prince Jin of Yong recommended Kui.

sentences.zh: 與諸州所舉五十餘人謁見，高祖望夔謂侍臣：「唯此一人，稱吾所舉。

translations.literal: Together with more than fifty men recommended from the various provinces he had audience; the Founder gazed at Kui and said to the attending ministers: "Only this one man fits what I recommended."
translations.idiomatic: Of more than fifty candidates presented, Emperor Wen singled out Kui, telling his ministers, "Only this one is what I had in mind."

sentences.zh: 」於是拜晉王友。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he was appointed Friend of the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed friend to Prince Jin.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，遷太子洗馬，轉司朝謁者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was promoted to Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Court Receptionist.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he became palace attendant to the heir apparent, then court receptionist.

sentences.zh: 以父免職，夔亦去官。

translations.literal: Because his father was dismissed from office, Kui also left his post.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was disgraced, he resigned as well.

sentences.zh: 後曆尚書職方郎、燕王司馬。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Bureau Chief of the Ministry of War and Marshal of the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as bureau chief in the Ministry of War and marshal to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，夔領宿衛，以功拜朝散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign Kui headed night guard and for merit was appointed Grand Master of Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he commanded night guard and was rewarded with the title grand master of the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 時帝方勤遠略，蠻夷朝貢，前後相屬。

translations.literal: At the time the sovereign was just then laboring at distant campaigns; barbarians of the four directions came to court in tribute, one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pursuing campaigns abroad, and tributary missions arrived in succession.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容謂宇文述、虞世基等曰：「四夷率服，觀禮華夏，鴻臚之職，須歸令望。

translations.literal: The sovereign once at leisure said to Yuwen Shu, Yu Shiji, and others: "The four barbarians all submit; they come to observe ritual in Huaxia — the office of the Imperial Stud must return to a man of fine reputation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked to Yuwen Shu and Yu Shiji, "With the barbarians submitting, the office that receives them requires a man of talent and presence."

sentences.zh: 甯有多才藝，美容儀，可以接對賓客者為之乎？

translations.literal: "Is there one with many talents and arts, fine appearance and bearing, who can receive and respond to guests — to do this?"
translations.idiomatic: "Is there someone accomplished, presentable, and fit to receive foreign envoys?"

sentences.zh: 」鹹以夔對。

translations.literal: All took Kui as the answer.
translations.idiomatic: They all named Kui.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，即日拜鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: The sovereign approved and that same day appointed him Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and that same day made him vice director of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 其年，高昌王曲伯雅來朝，朝廷妻以公主。

translations.literal: That year the King of Gaochang Qu Boya came to court; the court married him to a princess.
translations.idiomatic: That year the king of Gaochang, Qu Boya, came to court and was given an imperial princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 夔有雅望，令主婚焉。

translations.literal: Kui had elegant reputation; he was ordered to preside over the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, who enjoyed high repute, was appointed to oversee the wedding.

sentences.zh: 其後弘化、延安等數郡盜賊蜂起，所在屯結，夔奉詔巡撫關中。

translations.literal: Afterward Honghua, Yan'an, and several commanderies had bandits swarming; wherever they were they encamped in groups; Kui received an edict to tour and pacify Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels rose in Honghua, Yan'an, and other districts, he was sent to pacify Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 突厥之圍雁門也，夔領城東面事。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, Kui took charge of affairs on the city's east face.
translations.idiomatic: During the Turkish siege of Yanmen he commanded the eastern defenses.

sentences.zh: 夔為弩樓車箱獸圈，一夕而就。

translations.literal: Kui made crossbow towers, chariot boxes, and beast pens — in one night they were completed.
translations.idiomatic: He built crossbow towers, siege engines, and stockades in a single night.

sentences.zh: 帝見而善之，以功進位通議大夫。

translations.literal: The sovereign saw and approved; for merit he was advanced to Master of Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and promoted him to master of discussion.

sentences.zh: 坐父事，除名為民。

translations.literal: He sat in connection with his father's affair and was stripped of name and made commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was disgraced along with his father and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 複丁母憂，不勝哀而卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: He again encountered his mother's mourning, could not bear the grief and died; at the time his age was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He then lost his mother, grieved himself to death, and died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 史評史臣曰：齊公霸圖伊始，早預經綸，魚水冥符，風雲玄感。

translations.literal: The historians comment: The historians say: Duke of Qi at the start of his hegemonic design early participated in state planning; fish and water were darkly aligned, wind and clouds mysteriously responsive.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: When Duke of Qi's rise began, Gao Jiong was already at his side in perfect trust, like fish and water.

sentences.zh: 正身直道，弼諧與運，心同契合，言聽計從。

translations.literal: Correcting his person and walking the straight Way, he harmonized and aided with the age; hearts alike matched in union, words heard and plans followed.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and dutiful, he guided the founding of the dynasty in full accord with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 東夏克平，南國底定，參謀帷幄，決勝千里。

translations.literal: Eastern Xia was conquered and pacified, the southern state was settled; he counseled within the tent and decided victory a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: He planned the conquest of the south and the pacification of the east from the command tent.

sentences.zh: 高祖既複禹跡，思布堯心，舟楫是寄，鹽梅斯在。

translations.literal: The Founder had restored Yu's tracks and thought to spread Yao's heart; boats and oars were entrusted, salt and plums were there.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen restored order to the realm and relied on him as on the seasoning of governance.

sentences.zh: 兆庶賴以康寧，百僚資而輯睦，年將二紀，人無間言。

translations.literal: The hundred myriads relied on him for peace and tranquility; the hundred officials drew from him for harmony; years approached two reign periods, and among the people there was no dissenting speech.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years the people prospered and the bureaucracy was united, without a word of complaint.

sentences.zh: 屬高祖將廢儲宮，由忠信而得罪；

translations.literal: It happened that the Founder was about to depose the heir apparent; through loyalty and faith he met with offense;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor considered deposing the crown prince, Jiong was punished for his loyalty;

sentences.zh: 逮煬帝方逞浮侈，以忤時而受戮。

translations.literal: when Emperor Yang was just then indulging floating extravagance, he met execution for opposing the times.
translations.idiomatic: under Emperor Yang he was executed for opposing excess.

sentences.zh: 若使遂無猜釁，克終厥美，雖未可參縱稷、契，足以方駕蕭、曹。

translations.literal: If he had indeed had no suspicion or rancor and could have completed his excellence to the end, though he might not be compared with following Hou Ji and Xie, he would suffice to drive abreast with Xiao and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Had he lived out his career without falling victim to suspicion, he might have ranked with the greatest ministers of antiquity, beside Xiao He and Cao Can.

sentences.zh: 繼之實難，惜矣！

translations.literal: To continue him was truly difficult — how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: To find his equal would have been hard — a tragic loss.

sentences.zh: 邳公周道雲季，方事幽貞；

translations.literal: Duke of Pi — the Zhou Way's season was ending and he served secluded integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Pi Su Wei, in the twilight of the Zhou order, held to solitary integrity;

sentences.zh: 隋室龍興，首應旌命。

translations.literal: when the Sui house rose like a dragon, he first answered the banner and command.
translations.idiomatic: when the Sui arose he was among the first to answer the call.

sentences.zh: 綢繆任遇，窮極榮寵；

translations.literal: Intimate care and encounter reached the extreme of glory and favor;
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the summit of honor and trust;

sentences.zh: 久處機衡，多所損益；

translations.literal: long occupying the keys of state, in many matters brought benefit and harm;
translations.idiomatic: long held the reins of government and shaped policy for good and ill;

sentences.zh: 罄竭心力，知無不為。

translations.literal: exhausting heart and strength, wherever he knew, nothing was not done.
translations.idiomatic: he gave his utmost in everything he undertook.

sentences.zh: 然志尚清儉，體非弘曠，好同惡異，有乖直道，不存易簡，未為通德。

translations.literal: Yet his aim prized purity and frugality; his substance was not broad and vast; he liked agreement and hated difference, which had the defect of the straight Way; he did not preserve simplicity and ease — he was not a thorough virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was narrow in spirit, loved agreement and hated dissent, and lacked the breadth of true statesmanship.

sentences.zh: 曆事二帝，三十餘年，雖廢黜當時，終稱遺老。

translations.literal: He served two sovereigns for more than thirty years; though dismissed in his time, in the end he was called a surviving elder.
translations.idiomatic: He served two emperors for thirty years; though repeatedly disgraced, he was still revered as an elder statesman.

sentences.zh: 君邪而不能正言，國亡而情均眾庶。

translations.literal: The sovereign was wicked yet he could not speak correction; the state perished yet his feeling equaled the common multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler went astray he could not correct him; when the state fell he was no better than the crowd.

sentences.zh: 予違汝弼，徒聞其語；

translations.literal: "When I err, you assist me" — one only hears the words;
translations.idiomatic: "When I err, correct me" — he mouthed the saying,

sentences.zh: 疾風勁草，未見其人。

translations.literal: "In a fierce wind, the tough grass" — the man was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: but "the tough grass appears only in a high wind" — and the man was not seen.

sentences.zh: 禮命闕于興王，抑亦此之由也。

translations.literal: Ritual and command were lacking in the rising king — perhaps this too was the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The throne's failure to honor him in the founding may owe something to this.

sentences.zh: 夔志識沉敏，方雅可稱，若天假之年，足以不虧堂構矣。

translations.literal: Kui's aim and discernment were deep and keen, square and elegant enough to be praised; if Heaven had lent him years, he would have sufficed not to bring shame on the hall's structure.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was talented and accomplished; had he lived longer, he might have upheld the family name without disgrace.
